situation:
You are the brand communications manager at CROWNPOINT INSURANCE, a regional insurer whose name sits on the roof of a downtown arena that seats twelve thousand. The vice president of marketing (judge) has asked you to recommend how the company should run the group sales program it puts in front of its own agents and their clients at that arena next season.

Crownpoint bought the arena naming rights four years ago and merged with COPPERVALE MUTUAL last spring, and the two companies have not finished becoming one. Agents out of both books now sell side by side under the Crownpoint name, the two service centers still answer the phone in different words, and the merger's integration plan freezes new headcount until those centers are combined.

The group sales program is the most visible thing the naming rights buy. An agent invites clients to a block of seats on a group night, and the arena posts that night on its own channels. Under the naming rights agreement, anything carrying the arena's name needs the arena's approval before it goes out. Nothing in the program tells an agent what to say, and the merged agents are describing the same coverage in different terms.

The cheapest path is to let the merged agents promote group nights from their own social accounts, which costs nothing and leaves no one reviewing what they post, so a wrong claim about coverage would land on the company's name across the front of the arena. The other path is to fund a staffed group sales desk with one trained team that reviews every message, which means pulling the people and money out of service lines the merger has already stretched thin.

The vice president of marketing (judge) wants your recommendation on how the group sales program should be run next season, what the agents should be told to say and not to say about the coverage they sell, and how the company would find out afterward whether the choice worked. The vice president of marketing (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
